business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Subtitle Transcription and AI Voice Cloning Studio

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Estado español; no sub-state tax distinction; the Basque Country and Navarre foral regimes are expressly out of scope of this model)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European tradition; codified Commercial Registry system under Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 and Real Decreto 1784/1996; Latin notarial system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-Chile DTA (2003) and Spain-Chile BIT (1994); both aligned with the Latin America bridge mandate

EU Law: Treaty on the Functioning of the EU (free movement of capital, arts. 63-66 TFEU); EU Regulation 2019/452 on FDI screening; EU General Data Protection Regulation 2016/679 (relevant for AI/subtitle data flows)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, principally Articles 19-23 (formation deed and articles), 58-62 (capital contributions), 210-242 (directors and governance), and 246-251 (board procedures where applicable), as amended by Law 18/2022.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the province of the registered office, under the supervision of the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (escritura pública de constitución), including the company bylaws (estatutos sociales), filed for registration with the applicable Provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum share capital is EUR 1.00. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until the company reaches EUR 3,000 of capital, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders bear additional statutory liability on liquidation in specified circumstances. No statutory escrow account is required, although a bank certificate of deposit may be used where cash contributions are made.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that all subscribed shares stated in the incorporation deed are accepted as fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the deed and applicable law. The registered office is adopted at the address recorded in the deed, with authority delegated to the managing director to complete any lawful address formalities. The Board appoints [Name] as sole managing director, or, if a board structure is selected, appoints the stated officers and assigns their respective powers. The officers are authorized to obtain the tax identification number, open bank accounts, execute ordinary commercial contracts, and complete all Mercantile Registry, tax, municipal, and licensing filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its online name-certification service or authorized filing channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names in priority order. Obtain the negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social), which must identify the approved name and applicant. Use the approved name in the incorporation deed and complete incorporation within the certificate validity period.
required_dossiers: Intended legal form: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name or cure the similarity or prohibited-term issue. If the certificate expires, request a renewal where available or obtain a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Incorporation Documents and Capital Evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public selected for execution of the public incorporation deed; banking institution for voluntary capital-account evidence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the bylaws, shareholder details, share allocation, management structure, registered office, corporate purpose, beneficial-owner information, and evidence of contributions. Cash contributions must be fully paid at incorporation. A bank deposit certificate may be obtained, although statutory rules may permit the founders to state responsibility for the reality of cash contributions in the deed.
required_dossiers: Founders' passports or national identity documents
Spanish or foreign tax identification numbers, as applicable
Bank certificate or founders' contribution declaration
Powers of attorney, legalized and apostilled where required
Certified Spanish translations for non-Spanish documents where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct incomplete identity, ownership, capital, or beneficial-owner information. Re-execute or supplement the deed if the notary identifies a formal defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario) with jurisdiction to authenticate the incorporation deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders, or duly authorized representatives, sign the public deed before the notary. The notary verifies identity, capacity, corporate name, capital, contributions, bylaws, management appointment, and foreign-document formalities. Request an electronic authorized copy for registry filing and a simple copy for tax and banking procedures.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution evidence or statutory declaration
Foreign powers of attorney with apostille or legalization and translation, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve notarial observations before signature. If a post-signature correction is required, execute a corrective or supplementary public deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and File Incorporation Tax Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria), generally through Form 036 or the CIRCE/DUE system where eligible.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the provisional Spanish tax identification number (NIF), register the company for tax purposes, and submit the applicable incorporation-related tax declaration. The incorporation transaction is generally exempt from transfer and stamp duty under the relevant tax rules, but the declaration may still be required. Obtain the definitive NIF after Mercantile Registry registration.
required_dossiers: Corporate activity and tax classification details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a Tax Agency request with corrected Form 036, identity evidence, deed extracts, or proof of address. File any pending declaration within the cure period stated in the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered-office province, through its electronic or in-person filing desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authorized public deed, provisional NIF, name certificate, and required registry forms. Pay the registry charges applicable to the filing. Monitor the registry entry and collect the registered deed, definitive NIF evidence, and registry certificate or electronic extract.
required_dossiers: Authorized copy of the public incorporation deed
Proof of payment of registry charges
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a qualification defect notice, cure the defect by supplementary deed, corrected filing, missing document, or clarification within the applicable period. A negative qualification may be appealed administratively to the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith or challenged before the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Registration Governance and Operating Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry, Spanish Tax Agency, Social Security Treasury, and the relevant municipality or Autonomous Community authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the definitive NIF, legalize mandatory corporate books electronically through the Mercantile Registry, register the beneficial-owner book where required, file commencement and activity information, register as an employer if personnel are hired, and submit the applicable municipal opening or activity declaration for the premises. Establish accounting, invoicing, data-protection, labor, and audiovisual-rights compliance controls.
required_dossiers: Social Security employer registration, if applicable
Technical premises report and municipal declaration, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected electronic books, tax registrations, or municipal declarations. Suspend affected operations until any required municipal, fire, occupational, or premises deficiencies are remedied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No national industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for an AI subtitle transcription, post-production, or audio-dubbing studio. Where the premises contain regulated electrical, fire, lifting, pressure, or other industrial installations, the competent authority is the Industry Directorate of the relevant Autonomous Community, together with the municipality for premises authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Responsible Declaration for Opening and Activity (declaración responsable de apertura y actividad), or a municipal activity and opening licence where required by the applicable local ordinance. No general manufacturing permit applies to the stated business model.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), with implementation by the competent Autonomous Community environmental authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from national or regional project-level EIA under Law 21/2013 because ordinary digital post-production and dubbing activities are not listed projects. A municipal environmental qualification or activity assessment may still be required, depending on premises, equipment, noise, and local regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable municipal wastewater authorization and sewer limits; do not discharge hazardous substances without authorization. Manage electronic equipment, batteries, packaging, and other waste under Law 7/2022 and applicable producer and waste-transfer rules. If solvents, paints, or other VOC-emitting processes are introduced, assess Royal Decree 117/2003 and any Autonomous Community permit requirements. Control studio noise under applicable national, regional, and municipal limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the applicable municipal opening or activity clearance supported by a competent technician where required. Demonstrate compliance with the Technical Building Code, particularly fire safety requirements under DB-SI, and with the Regulation on Fire Safety in Industrial Establishments only if the premises qualify as an industrial establishment. Complete electrical and other regulated-installation certificates through authorized installers. Implement occupational risk prevention under Law 31/1995 and Royal Decree 486/1997, including workplace risk assessment, emergency procedures, evacuation arrangements, accessibility, load limits, and periodic maintenance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and official electronic portal at https://www.agenciatributaria.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL entities obtain NIF through AEAT registration via a registered gestor or legal representative. Required documents include incorporation certificate, passport copies of shareholders, and proof of domicile. Foreign-owned SLs follow identical procedure with apostilled documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available. Territorial tax regime is mandatory with no hybrid mismatch or entity classification elections permitted under Spanish law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing in Facturae XML format for all B2B transactions since 2021. Real-time reporting and digital stamping (sello electrónico) required via AEAT portal or integrated API for VAT-registered taxpayers exceeding certain thresholds.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods exported to third countries or services performed for non-residents where the service is effectively utilized outside Spain. Must substantiate with evidence of export or performance abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment received
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audits common; fraudulent claims result in full refund denial, fines up to 100% of improperly claimed VAT, criminal liability, and permanent disqualification from export zero-rating regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under the Eurozone fully convertible currency regime. Both current account and capital account transactions are freely convertible with no restrictions. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted after applicable Spanish withholding tax without FX surrender obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export proceeds surrender regime applies in Spain. Companies must file export declarations with the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for statistical and tax compliance purposes. There are no statutory timelines for conversion to domestic currency or mandatory ratios; voluntary surrender to banks is available upon request.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for cross-border electronic money institutions via licensed Spanish platforms such as Wise, subject to compliance with the Spanish Electronic Money Directive and MiCA regulations. Offshore digital EMIs face legal constraints including mandatory Spanish AML/KYC registration for any entity with Spanish operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding is permitted for Spanish SL companies using electronic signatures and video KYC. Physical presence of directors is not mandatory for standard corporate account opening, though video interviews may be required for enhanced due diligence or complex ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed beneficial ownership or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registro Mercantil certificate of incorporation and beneficial owners, share purchase agreements, and source of wealth declarations

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Links to high-risk jurisdictions or sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country risk assessments, PEP declarations, and transaction monitoring reports to demonstrate legitimate business purpose

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with purpose codes such as 'CAPCON' (capital contribution) or 'EQTY'. Verification requires shareholder resolutions, capital increase notifications filed with Registro Mercantil, and proof of funds origin. All must align with Spanish corporate law and tax filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements are cleared using SWIFT MT103 for international bank transfers. Commercial Letters of Credit (LCs) can be issued through correspondent banks. Given the service-oriented nature of subtitle production, settlements often utilize payment gateways like Stripe or Wise for client payments in supported currencies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts for EUR/USD hedging
Currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity management
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for clients with USD exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) at the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil of the province of the registered office (electronic filing via the Registradores portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General meeting approval no later than six months after year-end (30 June for calendar-year SL); deposit within one month after approval, normally by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit blocks registration of corporate acts in the Mercantile Registry until accounts are filed; omission is published in BORME and may attract administrative fines under Spanish accounting-registry rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalisation of Annual Accounting Books (Libros Contables)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the financial year-end, i.e. by 30 April for a calendar-year SL.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-legalised books lose evidential value in commercial and tax proceedings; the annual accounts deposit may be rejected by the registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days after six months following the tax-year end; calendar-year SL due by 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge under Art. 27 LGT (5% to 20% depending on delay), late-payment interest, and penalties under Art. 198 LGT if filed after formal AEAT requirement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year taxpayers: by 30 January following the tax period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission triggers Art. 27 LGT surcharge (5% to 20%), late-payment interest, and possible penalties under Art. 198 LGT.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statement of Transactions with Third Parties (Modelo 347) – conditional on volume
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window through 28 February following the tax year if aggregate annual transactions with any single counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing is subject to Art. 27 LGT surcharge, late-payment interest, and penalties under Art. 198 LGT.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate Beneficial Owner confirmation and Register of Members update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil / Registro de Titularidades Reales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO data confirmed with the annual accounts deposit by the regular deposit deadline (31 July for calendar-year SL); any share-transfer-driven change must be registered within one month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered share transfers and outdated UBO information block registration of subsequent corporate acts and may trigger AML administrative penalties under Law 10/2010.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SL is subject to mandatory independent audit if it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at year-end for two consecutive years: total assets above EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover above EUR 5,700,000; average workforce above 50 employees (art. 263 Ley de Sociedades de Capital).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, Real Decreto 1514/2007); eligible smaller entities may apply PGC Pymes under Real Decreto 1515/2007. IFRS-EU applies to consolidated accounts of listed groups and entities required to use it.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not impose a standalone annual confirmation statement for an SL. The SL must keep a current Register of Partners at the registered office; every transfer of participations must be recorded. UBO identification and current ownership are declared as part of the annual accounts deposit, and changes of beneficial ownership must be submitted to the Registro de Titularidades Reales / Mercantile Registry within one month.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas) covering shareholders' and directors' resolutions
Related-Party and Sole-Shareholder Contracts Book (Libro Registro de Contratos) where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 – 800 per year for registered office/registered agent and basic corporate maintenance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – 9,000 per audit for an SL that exceeds statutory audit thresholds; no audit fee required for a small SL below those thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Qualifying newly created entities are generally taxed at 15% in their first tax period with a positive taxable base and the following tax period. Additional reduced rates may apply according to company size, tax status, and applicable transitional rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying newly created entities may use the 15% rate described above. Spanish law also provides deductions for qualifying R&D and technological innovation, audiovisual productions, and certain other activities; eligibility, limits, certification, and regional rules must be checked for each claim. No general tax holiday applies to an ordinary Spanish SL.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite; Spain has no fixed-year expiry for tax loss carryforwards. Their use is subject to statutory limitations, including taxable-base limits and minimum utilization rules. The schema's five-year default does not reflect Spanish law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) e-filing service. Modelo 202 is generally used for advance corporate tax payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; advance payments are generally made in April, October, and December where required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 is due within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the ordinary filing period is 1–25 July. Modelo 202 advance payments are generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December, subject to statutory exceptions and payment-method rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identity, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), tax period, legal form, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned Spanish SL files as a Spanish-resident corporate taxpayer and uses its Spanish NIF. Disclose foreign ownership and related-party information where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result before tax, as reported in the statutory accounts, with required tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Spanish SL's worldwide accounting result; do not substitute the non-resident shareholder's income or the permanent-establishment rules applicable to a foreign company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary book-to-tax adjustments, tax-exempt income, non-deductible expenses, and resulting taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish corporate tax rules to the SL. Assess deductibility, withholding, and transfer-pricing treatment of payments to non-resident related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Available prior-period tax losses and the amount claimed against the current taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain evidence of origin and availability of losses and apply Spanish utilization limitations; ownership changes or inactive-company rules may restrict use.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate, credits, and incentives fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate, deductions, tax credits, and other relief claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim a reduced rate or incentive only where the SL meets the statutory conditions and retains supporting records or required certifications.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, withholding credits, other payments on account, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Spanish payments and credits to AEAT records. Treaty relief for shareholder-level withholding is not a credit in the SL's Modelo 200 merely because its shareholder is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions and other disclosures required by the return and applicable Spanish regulations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify cross-border related-party dealings, including services, royalties, financing, and intellectual property arrangements; separately assess Modelo 232 reporting obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a prior AEAT request generally attracts a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each full month of delay; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest. If the return shows no tax due or a refund, fixed penalties may apply, generally reduced where statutory conditions are met. An incorrect return may trigger tax-geared penalties, commonly 50% to 150% of the underpaid amount depending on the conduct and its severity. Late payment can also incur surcharges and interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish domestic withholding rate on dividends paid to non-residents, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. A qualifying EU parent may be exempt under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, generally subject to a minimum direct holding of 5% and a one-year holding-period condition, together with other statutory requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, provide the Spanish payer with a valid tax residence certificate issued by the competent authority of the recipient's residence state and any required beneficial-ownership and eligibility evidence. The payer applies the relevant treaty rate or exemption and reports the payment and withholding through the applicable Spanish forms. If excess tax is withheld, the recipient generally claims a refund from AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure. Treaty entitlement depends on the specific treaty, limitation provisions, and facts; a certificate alone does not establish beneficial ownership or eligibility.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general Spanish non-resident withholding rate is 19% for interest and royalties, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable treaties. Qualifying interest and royalties paid between associated companies in different EU Member States may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, subject to ownership, holding-period, beneficial-owner, and anti-abuse conditions. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and income classification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Generally, Spanish transfer-pricing documentation is not required for transactions with the same related party where the aggregate consideration for the tax period does not exceed EUR 250,000, subject to statutory exceptions. Transactions involving specified tax-haven jurisdictions, certain individual transactions, and other excluded categories may remain subject to documentation or reporting rules. Separate Modelo 232 reporting thresholds and exceptions apply.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply a standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Spanish transfer-pricing, anti-abuse, beneficial-ownership, controlled-foreign-company, and general anti-avoidance rules may nevertheless challenge arrangements lacking commercial rationale, personnel, decision-making, or functions consistent with the reported profits. Substance and documentation requirements depend on the facts and applicable rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing income, fabricating deductions, maintaining false accounts, or otherwise intentionally evading Spanish tax where the evaded amount exceeds the criminal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax fraud involving an amount exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax and tax period may constitute a criminal offence under the Spanish Criminal Code. The basic offence can carry imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of up to six times the amount defrauded, in addition to tax, interest, and related consequences. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or other statutory circumstances, carry more severe penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or other responsible individuals may face criminal liability if they participate in, authorize, or knowingly facilitate the offence. A corporate penalty does not automatically pierce the corporate veil; personal liability requires a statutory basis and proof of the individual's conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False or incomplete tax returns and accounting records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting materially inaccurate returns, omitting taxable income, claiming unsupported deductions, or failing to maintain legally required accounting and tax records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties depend on the conduct, culpability, and tax loss; tax-geared penalties commonly range from 50% to 150% of the underpaid tax, with late-payment interest and recovery of the tax due. Separate penalties may apply for accounting, invoicing, or information-reporting breaches.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal administrative or criminal exposure where statutory requirements for participation, negligence, or culpable conduct are met. Ordinary corporate tax debts do not automatically become personal debts of an SL's directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party transactions other than at arm's length, omitting required documentation, or failing to make required related-party disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may adjust taxable income and impose statutory penalties for transfer-pricing documentation and valuation breaches. Penalties depend on the type of breach and may apply per data item or as a percentage of the adjustment; tax, interest, and general tax penalties may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director liability is not automatic. It may arise where the director personally participates in fraud or where statutory rules establish responsibility for the relevant tax or reporting breach.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful profit distribution or withholding-tax failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits contrary to Spanish company-law restrictions, failing to withhold or remit tax on dividends, interest, or royalties, or claiming treaty relief without satisfying its conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company may owe the unwithheld tax, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties. An unlawful distribution may be recoverable under Spanish company law and may also create director liability under the statutory rules governing unlawful distributions and director duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for repayment or damages where statutory conditions are met, including knowingly approving or executing an unlawful distribution. Liability is fact-specific and does not arise solely from non-resident ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and concealment of beneficial ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly handling proceeds of crime, disguising ownership or source of funds, or failing to meet applicable customer-due-diligence, recordkeeping, or reporting duties as an obliged entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Applicable sanctions under Spanish anti-money-laundering law depend on the conduct and severity and may include substantial administrative fines, restrictions, and, for laundering conduct, criminal penalties under the Criminal Code. A business's status as an obliged entity depends on its activities; an ordinary subtitle-production studio is not automatically an obliged entity solely because it uses Stripe or Wise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals may face personal administrative or criminal liability for their own participation or for statutory non-compliance attributable to them. Imprisonment, travel restrictions, or asset measures require an applicable legal basis and competent-authority or court action; they are not automatic consequences of a compliance breach.
